Kento Alpha 0.9.8, build 2451

The color picker

  • Every color swatch opens Kento's own color picker: a square of saturation and value beside a hue strip, drawn as your display shows them.
  • RGB (with alpha, where the color has one) and HSV are linear values, as the comp works in them, and can go past 1. The menu at the end of the hex row shows them in another of the config's spaces; the knob always gets the working space.
  • hex is the color as the display shows it; type a code to set it.
  • Pick from the Viewer: a point, or the average of an area you drag, of the picture coming into the node (before) or the one it makes (after).
  • Screen... opens the system's color window, to pick from anywhere on the screen.
  • recent keeps the last six colors you chose; swatches are your own (+ adds one, right-click removes it). Both are kept with your preferences.

The Viewer

  • The input process works, as in Nuke: name any image node VIEWER_INPUT (a grade, a group) and the Viewer shows its picture through it, for the eye only. IP on bar 1 turns it off and on. The pixel readout and the scopes read the picture itself. A .nk keeps a Viewer's IP turned off and another node's name.

Motion

  • The Motion window's Edit works: the motion as Nuke's expression, to change as you like; Apply writes it onto the knobs, curve standing for the knob's own keys.
  • Each setting of a motion (amplitude, frequency, roughness...) can be linked to another knob with the link button at the end of its row: the motion follows that knob, live, and a bake keeps its values.

The Node Graph

  • ⌥H (Edit > Node > Hide input) hides a node's input wire, leaving a short stub at the input; it shows dashed while the node or its source is selected. The Node tab's hide input does the same, and a .nk's hide input comes in and goes back.
  • ⌘F7 to ⌘F10 keep the Node Graph's view, zoom and group; ⇧F8 to ⇧F10 go back to them (the first from Edit > Node Graph location).
  • ⇧⌘B bookmarks the selected nodes.
  • ⌥↑ and ⌥↓ (Edit > Node > Version up and down) step the selected Reads to their next or previous version on disk, and Writes one version on or back.

Tracking

  • A track handed over shows the point it lost in a dashed box, "lost at" its frame, and, selected, a card saying when it was handed over and the offset kept.

Roto

  • Per-point feather, under Selected shape on the Roto tab: how far the point picked in the Viewer has its feather point, in pixels. Change it and the feather moves along the way it stands out, or straight out from the shape for a point with no feather yet.
  • The Dope Sheet opens a Roto or RotoPaint into its shapes and strokes, each with its tool's icon and its lifetime as a bar in its color: drag an end to change that frame, or the bar to slide it. This frame keeps only what's drawn at the current frame.
  • Freehand (⇧V) draws a shape by hand: drag round the outline and it becomes a smooth Bezier.

Report a problem

  • A report filed in the studio bug tracker now takes its .zip with it (the comp, every picture, the voice note), up to 100 MB; a bigger one stays on your Mac and the note says so.
  • Help > My reports shows how each filed report stands in the tracker: Open, In progress, Resolved or Won't fix, with the pipeline team's reply under it.

The look

  • Each pane's menu (split, float, its panels) is a small icon at the end of its tab row, where a blank square was. The Viewers panel, alone in its pane, shows one row: its strip, with the same icon.
  • One error red everywhere: a node's error glow and the error card use the same red.
  • The transport's buttons are outlines: bars and triangles at the ends, a chevron a frame either way.
  • A Read's Colour tab says what its file tells of its color: file type, bit depth, what the file says, the rules that match, every guess, and what it's read as.

Fixes

  • The Dope Sheet's rows follow an undo at once (a shape's keys moved back showed where they had been).
  • The Timeline under the Viewer is never cut off: in a narrow window its transport line shows in full below the ruler, and so does its sound lane.

Color

  • A Nuke script saved back from Kento writes the kinds you chose in This comp > Colour > Reading files by kind as its Project Settings' LUTs.

The manual

  • Every guide chapter now starts with a Try it; the keyboard shortcuts chapter's shows how to look a key up and give a free key an action.
  • The getting-started chapters have them too: make room for the picture and put the window back, save and version up a comp, find a key and a node's help. Getting help's page on reporting a problem now matches the window.

Kento Alpha 0.9.7, build 2416

The Read's panel

  • A quiet line under a Read's name says what its file is: its size, frames and layers, such as "1920 x 1080, 1001 to 1096, 3 layers".
  • version steps the file's version with its arrows, only to versions that have files on disk. Every "v002" in the path changes at once, the folder's and the file's, as one undo.
  • Make relative beside the version writes the file from the comp's folder ("../plates/..."); Make full writes it in full again.
  • The frame range is one row: the first frame and what shows before it, then the last frame and what shows after it.
  • Rescan beside the original range reads the folder again; the frame range follows when it was the old original range.
  • A ? beside the input transform says how the Read's color space was chosen, or what the file itself says when it was set by hand.
  • The format row reads "1920 x 1080, from the file", and the panel's labels are lower case, as designed.

Color

  • The Viewer's look menu, after the view, shows a look from the comp's config, or a session CDL loaded from a .cc, .cdl or .ccc file, before the display and view. For the eye only, and not saved with the comp; playing from the cache shows it too.
  • This comp > Colour > Reading files by kind sets the color space for 8-bit, 16-bit, log, float and movie files that don't say what they are, with use the config's file rules first. They're saved with the comp, and the comp panel's Colour tab has them too. A Nuke script opened in Kento brings its Project Settings' LUTs for each kind there.

Formats

  • Formats... beside the comp's format lists every format the menus offer. Add your own (name, width, height, pixel aspect) or remove them; yours are kept with your preferences and are in every format menu.
  • A size named in a format menu's Custom size... is kept the same way.

On-screen controls

  • A Transform's jack takes the transform's scale and skew, as the picture does: scaled more in x than y, its circle is an ellipse; skewed, it leans. It keeps its size on screen.

The Node Graph's settings

  • Settings > Node Graph > Wires is laid out as designed: Direct or Routed, Hop, Gap or Plain, and Off, Selected nodes or All for linked values, side by side; the thickness as a field and a slider, with a strip showing each kind of line at that thickness; the checks paired on a row each.

Focus mode

  • While a panel fills the window, the pane's tabs and menu square hide, and so does the Viewers panel's row of tabs.
  • Settings > Interface > Focus: keep the tool bars, the transport, its timeline, and its frame and fps, each on or off; hide the controls after a number of seconds; panels slide in from the edge, open only on a click or key, or stay hidden; and dim the image behind a panel that has slid in.

The Timeline

  • Client notes, the toggle beside Marks, shows the shot's review notes on the ruler: a yellow tick at each frame a note names, a white dot under it when the note has drawing there. Point at one for its words, who wrote it and when. The comp must be saved in a shot's folder.

Sound

  • While stopped, moving the playhead plays a moment of the comp's sound there, so you can find a beat by ear. Scrub the sound in the audio lane's menu, or Preferences > Viewer > Playback, turns it off.

Report a problem

  • the last minute goes with a report: your undo steps and the log's lines from the minute before the window opened, as text, so what just happened can be sent without having recorded it.

Fixes

  • A Nuke script saved back from Kento keeps its color management (the OCIO config, working space and LUTs): an ACES script no longer opens in Nuke on Nuke's default config. A comp whose config you changed in Kento leaves them out.
  • A rec709 show's Reads read as Rec.709 in their pixels, not only in what the panel said, even when another comp had read the same file first.

Kento Alpha 0.9.6, build 2394

Report a problem and Suggest a feature

  • Help > Report a problem is now one window for two kinds: Report a problem and Suggest a feature. The studio's bug tracker files a suggestion as a feature request.
  • Add pictures to a report: Grab the window, Grab a panel (click the panel), Paste a picture (or press Cmd-V, or drop a picture on the window). Click a picture to mark it up with arrows, boxes, a pen and words in four colors.
  • Record voice adds a voice note of up to five minutes. macOS asks for the microphone the first time.
  • Watch me records Kento's window while you show the problem, with your clicks, keys and undo steps marked, and adds the movie to the report. Only Kento's window is recorded.
  • Goes with it lists what's sent, each part with its size and the total.
  • Every node error's card has Report this, which opens a report with the error's words and a picture of the window already in it.
  • Help > My reports lists what this Mac has sent, and whether each was filed or only saved.

The Viewer

  • Refresh on bar 2 reads the comp's files again, as Nuke's Reload does.
  • A Rulers button on bar 2.
  • The zoom menu has Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit width, Fit height and 400%.
  • Downscale while playing: the Viewer can play at a smaller size and show full size when it stops.
  • Fit to an area on the data row now works: near and far from the region of interest or the part in view.
  • The guides popup shows "%" on its percentages, a sign on offsets, and the name of the preset in use.
  • Shift-1 to Shift-0 put that input on the B side of the compare, as in Nuke.
  • The compare menu's Lock B to A's frame: turn it off to hold B at a frame and compare it with others as you play.
  • The zoom menu's Lock zoom when switching inputs: turn it off and each input fits the view as it's shown.
  • Click the readout after R G B A to choose what it reads: HSVL, 8-bit, hex, log or spotmeter.
  • Cmd-click a pixel and the info bar keeps reading it; Cmd-Shift-drag a box to read its average. Click the lit eyedropper, or press Esc, to let go.
  • The layer menu ends with Other channels...: every channel in the image, to show any one on its own.
  • With a depth layer shown, one Z chip replaces RGB to Y, a label on the picture names the pass and its range, and the info bar gives the range too.

The Node Graph

  • The toolbar's Links menu shows linked values' lines for the selected nodes, all nodes or none. Option-E turns them off and back on.
  • A 3D scene's wire, from a card, camera or light, is drawn as a long dash and a dot.
  • Arrowheads at inputs, a new preference, puts a small arrowhead where each wire arrives.
  • An empty mask input ends in a short stub and an open ring, and a disabled node shows the picture passing straight through it.
  • Pressing a button on the node toolbar lights it by brightness, no longer yellow.
  • A Shuffle's tile names its layer, and a group's tile counts its nodes.
  • A selected Viewer node that isn't the one shown keeps a dimmer ring, so it's easy to tell from the shown one.
  • Click a Viewer node's number badge to give it another number.

Favourites

  • The star at the top of the node toolbar opens your Favourites: the nodes you make most, with their keys. Click one to add it; drag to reorder. Right-click a node in the toolbar's menus or in Tab search and choose Add to Favourites.

Properties

  • A control's menu has Copy value, Paste value and Paste as link.
  • The mouse wheel steps a number field you're typing in, as the arrow keys do.
  • Drag a control's label left or right to change its number, as you would drag its field.
  • A menu of ten choices or more opens with a find field and finds as you type: in a Merge, type "scr" for screen.
  • A Merge's operation menu lists the ten most used first, each with its formula, then all of them A to Z; the chosen formula shows beside it.
  • Panel tabs and headers name nodes as Nuke does: Merge, Shuffle and Tracker rather than Merge2, Shuffle2 and Tracker4, and the Sampler's first tab reads Sampler.
  • The pick-whip draws a dotted rope that swings as you drag and lights up over what it can link to. Dropped on a node in the Node Graph, it opens Kento's own menu of that node's controls.
  • The Sampler's Sample current button is lit, says which frame it read, and keeps its curves under a Curves header.
  • Roto Layers shows the off switch on the selected row.

Matching Nuke

  • Roto draws curved shapes as Nuke does, cutting each curve into as many straight pieces as Nuke uses for its length. Curved Roto edges, and transitions' edge lines, now match Nuke much more closely.
  • A tapering feather is drawn as Nuke draws it.
  • STMap and a corner pin under strong perspective filter each pixel as Nuke does.
  • GridWarp keeps its source's channels: an RGB plate stays RGB.
  • A Roto with no input covers only its shapes, as in Nuke.
  • In a show set to Rec.709, a Read whose file doesn't say its color space, and isn't a float file, starts as Rec.709. The panel says so.

Files, paths and movies

  • A comp saved on Windows finds its files on a Mac with no path maps set: Kura's drive is built in, whatever its drive letter.
  • ProRes movies and movies with alpha play much faster: an HD ProRes frame takes about 16 ms instead of 150.
  • Renders with badly named frames (a Fusion Saver's name.####0991.png) load as one sequence. The Shots panel marks them in amber.
  • The open and save dialogs show a picture of a comp saved in Kento, and each recent folder says when it was last used.
  • The footage browser lists a file's versions newest first.
  • Project settings can lock the frame range, so footage you bring in doesn't change it. A .nk's lock range is kept.
  • Bentos > Import gizmo... imports a gizmo, as File > Import does.
  • Relink's Choose a folder and Later are plain text buttons, as designed.

Shots and feedback

  • A Feedback panel beside Properties shows the shot's Kitsu notes.
  • The Shots panel's list matches the Nuke panel's: short names with their details beside them, and the sequence and shot menus apart.
  • Artists who aren't Kitsu admins can look up their shots.
  • Image Info (Gaffer's Image Inspector) is drawn in Kento's style.

Settings and plain words

  • Every setting's explanation has been rewritten in plain words, saying what it does for you.
  • A node's error card explains a missing color space, an unreadable file, an unset variable and a mistake in an expression, with ways to fix each.
  • This comp > Render's disk cache and threads say Change in Preferences: they're the same for every comp.
  • The Timeline's playback chip opens a panel: Loop, Ping-pong or Once side by side, Speed, a Frame rate field that takes any rate, and Show: frames, timecode or both.

Keys

  • Nuke's F5 renders all Writes, F12 clears the image cache, Option-` opens the Curve Editor, Option-Cmd-A selects connected nodes, and Option-G goes to a frame.

Fixes

  • Report a problem's grabs, Watch me and the comp pictures in the open dialog read only Kento's own window: a window in front of Kento's never gets in.
  • Opening a comp into a running Kento no longer crashes it.
  • Viewer > Background and Compare tick the choice you make.
  • Clicking the format in the Viewer's info bar opens Project settings again.
  • No more "already deleted" messages in the log after switching workspaces.
